meta.title: Siaya County: further analytical layers calculated from published figures (wage bill, development share, own-source revenue on three bases, department absorption, pending bills burden)
meta.label: Calculated by Takwimu Kenya from published figures
meta.rule: Every result is arithmetic on values already in the repository; each input names its dataset, record, value, unit, source and page, so a rejected input withholds the result (lib/review-status.js). Numerator and denominator come from the same document; series from different sources are never blended or averaged; a missing or non-comparable input gives a gap record with its reason. Thresholds are shown beside results as facts about the ratio, not verdicts.

families.B1: Wage bill as a share of total revenue (Controller of Budget, own-year report), beside the 35 per cent ceiling; the Auditor-General's own ratios beside, separate
families.B2: Development share of the budget (programme-based budgets, the County Treasury's review, the Controller of Budget) and of actual spending, beside the 30 per cent floor
families.B3: Own-source revenue against target, in real terms (FY 2024/25 prices) and per person, one series per source; FY 2024/25 on cash and accrual bases
families.B4: Absorption by department: actual spending over the final budget, same CBROP table
families.B5: Pending bills as a share of total revenue (Controller of Budget, own-year report), beside the 20 per cent limit the Auditor-General applies; the auditor's ratio beside

conventions.money: KSh million unless the unit says otherwise; KSh inputs divided by 1,000,000 and KSh billion multiplied by 1,000.
conventions.rounding: Percentages and KSh million to 2 decimals; per-person KSh to whole shillings.
conventions.fiscal_year_matching: A calendar-year population for year Y is paired only with FY Y/Y+1; nothing is interpolated.
conventions.same_document: Readings of one measure in one document within 1 per cent are the same figure (the most precise is used, the others listed); more than 1 per cent apart gives a gap.

meta.review: Provisional: awaiting editorial review. A result is approved only when it and every input are approved (lib/review-status.js).

records.title: Wage bill as a share of total revenue, FY 2013/14 (cob-report-2013-14)
records.formula: Wage bill (compensation of employees) divided by total revenue received (equitable share + conditional grants or additional allocations + own-source revenue), times 100. All from the Controller of Budget's report for the year.
records.caveat: Revenue here is what the Controller of Budget reports as received; it leaves out balances brought forward. The Auditor-General's ratios use the auditor's own denominator (receipts or revenue of the County Executive) and are shown beside, not combined.

threshold.rule: Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015, regulation 25(1)(b): expenditure on wages and benefits not to exceed 35 per cent of the county government's total revenue. Wording as commonly cited; the regulations are not yet in the source library.

beside.measure: Auditor-General finding (ratio as the auditor reports it)
beside.basis: The auditor's own ratio and denominator; not recomputed here.

comparability_notes: Stock scope: county executive.
records.caveat: Each stock the report prints is a separate record (scope and the bills of the year as the report states them); the Auditor-General's ratio counts total liabilities against the auditor's own revenue figure. Ageing (share older than a year) needs the Auditor-General's annexes, not yet transcribed.

threshold.rule: The Auditor-General tests total liabilities against 20 per cent of revenue (FY 2024/25 report on the County Executive); the limit as the auditor applies it, not a ratio defined in this repository.

records.title: Pending bills as a share of total revenue, FY 2024/25 (cob-report-2024-25, L256)
records.formula: Pending bills at 30 June (own-year report) divided by total revenue received in the year (equitable share + grants + own-source revenue, same report), times 100.
